description:
Project: Regional failover automation upgrade (Reliability Program: SLOs, incident reduction, graceful degradation)

Goals
- Reduce customer-visible impact from regional degradation/outages by upgrading failover triggers from mostly manual/heuristic processes to auditable, automated, safety-guarded orchestration.
- Validate new triggers and automation with controlled failover tests (game days) in staging and production (low-risk scopes first), and integrate learnings into runbooks, dashboards, and on-call processes.
- Improve graceful degradation behaviors during partial regional impairment (e.g., controlled load shedding, model variant fallback, queue/timeout tuning) so the platform stays “degraded but available” instead of failing hard.

Scope (in)
- Health-signal aggregation: define and standardize region health indicators (error rate, tail latency, upstream dependency health, capacity saturation, network path health).
- Trigger evaluation + orchestration: implement a trigger engine with thresholds, windows, hysteresis, and “safe-to-failover” checks; support progressive failover (subset of traffic, by customer tier/route/model).
- Automation paths: DNS/edge routing changes, internal routing policy updates, and capacity checks for target regions.
- Observability: metrics + dashboards for health signals, failover state machine, and customer impact; alert tuning aligned to SLO/error budget burn.
- Operational readiness: runbooks, incident bot integration, change management, release gating, and post-test retrospectives.

Scope (out)
- Major re-architecture of the data plane; this project focuses on automation and policy/triggering rather than rewriting the routing stack.
- Customer-facing feature commitments beyond reliability improvements (except where needed for comms and enterprise assurance).

Key stakeholders and teams
- Executive sponsor: Neha Kapoor (VP Infrastructure & Reliability)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (Dir SRE), Rafael Mendes (SRE Manager), Miles Thornton, Aisha Bello, Tomáš Novák
- Platform/Routing: Priya Natarajan (VP Eng Platform), Mina Haddad (EM Smart Routing), Vikram Singh
- Platform Control Plane: Ethan Park
- Infra/Fleet/Networking: Irene Choi (Dir Infra Eng), Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet), Harish Reddy (Capacity Ops)
- Release coordination: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
- Customer-facing escalation inputs (as-needed): Support/CS via Jira SUP tickets; occasional enterprise technical deep dives

Phases and rough timeline (hypothetical)
1) Discovery (1–2 weeks): incident review, define top failure modes and missing signals; draft trigger policy and safety constraints.
2) Build (3–6 weeks): implement health aggregation + trigger engine + orchestration hooks; add metrics, dashboards, and alert rules; feature flag + staged rollout.
3) Validation (2–4 weeks): staging game day(s), then production controlled failovers with strict guardrails and comms templates.
4) Rollout and hardening (ongoing): expand coverage to more services/routes/tiers; tune thresholds based on error budget and real-world behavior; complete runbook and training updates.

Constraints / risk management
- Avoid “flappy” failovers: hysteresis, hold-down timers, and manual override required.
- Prevent unsafe failovers: capacity and dependency checks in target region; canary % failover first.
- Change management: release gating, on-call approvals, and clear rollback procedures.
- Enterprise expectations: documented behavior and comms plans for controlled tests and real incidents.

Primary deliverables
- Confluence design/ADR(s), runbooks, game day plans, and updated SLO/error budget pages
- Linear initiative + execution issues with acceptance criteria
- GitHub PRs across routing/control plane, infra automation (terraform/helm), observability, and incident tooling
- Slack coordination threads for incidents, reviews, and game days
- A small number of support tickets/emails/calls reflecting escalations and customer assurance work

files.description: Program overview page: motivation from recent regional incidents, goals/non-goals, ownership (SRE + Smart Routing), milestones, risk controls, and links to Linear project + key runbooks.
ADR documenting decision to introduce a centralized trigger evaluation engine (signals, thresholds, hysteresis), safety checks (capacity/dependency), manual override policy, and audit requirements.
Service page describing the failover orchestrator/state machine, APIs/events, dependencies (routing policy store, DNS/edge, capacity signals), and operational characteristics.
Standard for region health signals: synthetic probes, network path checks, upstream dependency health, and how signals are published/consumed by the trigger engine.
Updated SLO definitions for multi-region availability and latency, plus error budget burn alerting guidance tied to automated mitigations and controlled failover tests.
Spec for new dashboards: region health overview, failover state transitions, customer impact by tier, plus alert rules and paging thresholds aligned with the new trigger signals.
Game day plan: hypotheses, blast radius, step-by-step test procedure for controlled failover, success criteria, stop conditions, comms plan, and roles (incident commander, observers).
Runbook for automated failover: how to enable/disable, interpret state, override triggers, rollback, and post-action verification checks (SLO recovery, queue drain, capacity).
Internal comms templates for controlled failover tests: status page language, support macros, and customer escalation guidance (what customers may see and how to respond).
Incident review synthesis focusing on trigger gaps (late detection, noisy signals, manual steps), with a prioritized list of reliability investments feeding this project.
Linear initiative umbrella issue (or top-level ticket) for “Regional failover automation upgrade”: scope, milestones, success metrics (MTTR reduction, incident count), and cross-team dependencies.
Define region health signal contract: required metrics, sampling windows, publishing mechanism, and acceptance criteria (coverage across hosted + dedicated).
Implement health signal aggregator service/job: ingestion, normalization, and persistence; includes backfill/testing plan and failure handling.
Add trigger evaluation logic (thresholds, hysteresis, hold-down timers) and state machine transitions; includes unit/integration tests.
Add “safe-to-failover” checks: target region capacity, dependency health, and routing policy sanity checks; define explicit stop conditions.
Progressive failover support: canary % routing, customer-tier scoping, route/model scoping; acceptance criteria includes rollback at any stage.
Observability: emit failover metrics/events and create initial dashboards; includes alert tuning and runbook links.
Incident bot integration: post state transitions and recommended actions into #incidents; include audit trail linkouts.
Terraform automation for routing/DNS primitives needed by orchestrator; includes review with infra/networking and staged rollout plan.
Staging game day execution: checklist, assigned roles, pre/post validation steps, and retro notes captured as comments.
Production controlled failover (low-risk slice): go/no-go criteria, comms checklist, monitoring plan, and post-test analysis requirements.
Graceful degradation behaviors during impaired region: load shedding policy, timeouts, fallback model variants, and customer-tier protections.
PM task: customer-facing narrative for reliability improvements (no over-promising), coordination with Support/CS for macros and escalation handling.
Post-rollout retro + threshold tuning: compare expected vs observed behavior, adjust signals/thresholds, and file follow-ups for remaining gaps.
PR: Introduce failover trigger evaluation module (thresholds, windows, hysteresis) behind a feature flag; includes tests and initial config schema.
PR: Add failover orchestrator state machine and audit log entries for transitions; includes manual override endpoints and RBAC checks.
PR: Implement progressive failover (percentage-based routing) with rollback support; updates routing policy evaluation and metrics.
PR: Add safe-to-failover capacity checks (GPU pool headroom, queue depth) and dependency gating; includes failure-mode tests.
PR: Graceful degradation controls (load shedding, tightened timeouts, fallback model variant selection) when region health is degraded but not failed.
PR: New dashboards/alerts for failover signals and state transitions; adds burn-rate alerts mapped to the multi-region SLO.
PR: Post failover state changes into #incidents with links to dashboards/runbook; add commands to query current failover mode.
PR: Add synthetic failover canary scenario (simulate partial regional impairment) and report expected recovery times/metrics.
PR: Terraform modules for health-check based routing/DNS records used by automated failover; includes environment-specific safeguards.
PR: Helm values/config wiring for failover orchestrator and signal aggregator; documents required secrets and rollout steps.
PR: Add multi-window/multi-burn alerts and a small tool to correlate failover actions with error budget impact.
PR: Add integration tests for failover rollback and hold-down timers; includes CI changes and flaky-test triage notes.
PR: Wire region health signal ingestion (synthetic probes + metrics) into aggregator; includes config validation and defaults.
PR: Document/configure optional multi-region failover controls for Private deployments (where supported), including operational caveats.
PR: Internal-facing documentation updates for new failover behavior, runbook references, and expected customer-visible symptoms during controlled tests.
Working doc with weekly notes, open questions, draft thresholds, links to dashboards/PRs, and coordination notes with Smart Routing and Infra.
Spreadsheet-style table: scenarios (partial outage, elevated 5xx, network partition), expected trigger outcome, stop conditions, and verification steps.
Checklist doc for game day execution: pre-flight (capacity, paging), step sequence, comms, observers, and post-flight validation.
Draft of dashboard layout, metric naming, and alert candidates; includes notes on what was too noisy in previous incidents.
Infra planning sheet: records/targets by region, TTL strategy, rollback approach, and change windows for controlled tests.
Early design draft (less polished than Confluence): state machine sketch, API ideas, risks, and alternatives considered.
Release plan draft: flag stages, guardrails, required sign-offs, and how to coordinate with on-call for enabling in prod.
Template for analyzing controlled failover results: timelines, impact, alert behavior, gaps, and follow-up actions.
Slack incident thread: regional degradation detected, discussion of whether/when to fail over, manual mitigations attempted, and decision points that motivate automation.
Slack incident thread: failover attempt coordination (routing/DNS), capacity concerns in target region, and post-mitigation validation checks.
SRE planning thread: enumerate health signals, debate thresholds/hysteresis, and agree on initial acceptance criteria for trigger engine.
Platform/SRE thread: progressive failover proposal (by route/customer tier), concerns about policy complexity, and decision to gate behind feature flag.
Infra networking thread: synthetic probes and network path health checks; discussion of false positives and where to run probes.
On-call coordination thread: runbook edits needed for automated failover, how to handle manual override, and paging policy updates.
Architecture discussion thread: trade-offs between centralized trigger service vs distributed per-component triggers; links to draft ADR.
SRE thread: error budget burn alerts mapping to automated actions; debate on alert sensitivity vs flappiness.
Thread: implement “safe-to-failover” capacity checks; clarifies which capacity signals are authoritative and who owns them.
Thread: Terraform/edge routing change management concerns; agreement on review requirements and change windows for game day.
Thread: game day scheduling, roles assignment (IC, comms, observers), and checklist finalization.
Thread: staging game day live coordination (simulate impairment, observe trigger behavior), plus quick fixes and follow-up tasks.
Thread: post-game-day retro discussion—what worked, what was noisy, changes needed before production test.
Release coordination thread: go/no-go for enabling feature flag in production for a limited slice; required sign-offs and rollback plan.
Thread: production controlled failover execution for low-risk segment; real-time monitoring, decision to proceed/abort, and confirmation of recovery.
Announcement thread: internal note about upcoming controlled failover window(s), what teams should expect, and where to report issues.
Support/SRE coordination thread: aligning support macros and escalation handling during controlled tests; links to comms template.
Thread: tuning trigger thresholds after initial prod test; review of false positives/negatives and next iteration plan.
Thread: graceful degradation plan (load shed vs failover) and how routing should behave for different customer tiers.
Thread: capacity/fleet readiness for increased cross-region traffic during failover; identifies needed headroom and procurement lead time.
Thread: update on-call training and runbook walkthrough for new automation; Q&A from engineers on rotation.
Thread: small real incident where automation is observed in ‘monitor-only’ mode; discussion of why it would/wouldn’t have triggered failover.
Thread: finalize KPIs for project success (incident count by cause, MTTR, time-to-detection, avoided failovers) and reporting cadence.
Thread: request for audit trail requirements and how to store/display failover decisions for later incident review.
Thread: DNS TTL strategy for failover tests; mitigation for caching and propagation delays, and decision on conservative defaults.
Support ticket: customer reports elevated 5xx and timeouts in a specific region; investigation links to region health dashboards and notes trigger didn’t fire soon enough.
Support ticket: dedicated customer sees intermittent routing to degraded region; asks about automatic failover behavior and expected SLAs.
Support ticket: streaming disconnects correlated with regional packet loss; contains logs, mitigation steps, and link to planned failover automation improvements.
Internal helpdesk ticket: request to adjust paging routing/permissions for failover orchestrator controls (RBAC groups, who can override).
Email thread: Neha Kapoor + Sean Gallagher + Priya Natarajan aligning on game day scope, risk controls, and go/no-go criteria; includes links to Drive checklist and Confluence plan.
Email thread: platform leadership + release engineering discussing feature-flag rollout stages, required reviews, and rollback expectations.
Email thread: customer escalation follow-up (external recipients) summarizing reliability improvements in progress, expected behavior, and support escalation paths; ties back to recent SUP ticket.

Fireflies transcript: technical deep dive with an enterprise customer after a regional incident—questions on automated failover triggers, safety checks, and customer-visible behavior; action items for follow-up docs.
Fireflies transcript: internal cross-functional readout of the first production controlled failover test—what was observed, what needs tuning, and next steps.

CRM company record for an enterprise account impacted by regional issues: requirements for multi-region resiliency, security constraints, recent support tickets/meetings, and next steps referencing the failover upgrade.
